title: sessions: an index, a tree and a price
intent: The session log is append-only and honest, and that is all it is: there is no index, no way to list the sessions of a project, no way to resume one, no way to branch it, and no account of what it cost. The reference harnesses have all four, and a session that cannot be resumed is a session that was thrown away. This wave adds the index, the tree, the resume and the cost, and keeps the log append-only underneath.
checks: ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/test-yeah-state.el tests/unit/test-yeah-loop.el tests/unit/test-yeah-tools.el tests/unit/test-yeah-perm.el tests/unit/test-yeah-session.el tests/unit/test-yeah-compact.el tests/unit/test-yeah-undo.el tests/unit/test-yeah-acp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-emcp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-gptel.el tests/unit/test-yeah-subagent.el tests/unit/test-yeah-shell.el tests/unit/test-yeah-codes.el
objection: A tree of sessions is a second structure next to the log, and two structures drift: the tree says one thing and the log another.
refuted_by: A resumed session whose tree disagrees with its log, so that the continuation is built on a state that never existed.
